prompt: Why is agenda's project package called config rather than agenda?
hint: Think about the directory it sits in.

choices.text: Django refuses a package with the same name as the directory
choices.why: It would accept it; the problem is reading the imports.

choices.text: A second agenda inside agenda makes imports ambiguous to read
choices.why: Right. config says what the package holds.

choices.text: config is required by uv
choices.why: uv does not care what the package is called.

choices.text: The settings module must be called config.settings
choices.why: Any name works; DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE points at it.

prompt: You run migrate a second time on agenda right after the first. What happens?

choices.text: The 18 migrations run again and recreate the tables
choices.why: Applied migrations are recorded and skipped.

choices.text: It fails because the tables exist
choices.why: It never tries to create them again.

choices.text: Nothing: each migration is recorded once applied
choices.why: Right. Django keeps a table of the migrations it has run.

choices.text: It deletes db.sqlite3 and starts over
choices.why: migrate never deletes the database.

prompt: Which manage.py command would you run to catch a misspelled app name before any request does?

choices.text: diffsettings
choices.why: It prints settings; it does not import the apps to validate them.

choices.text: runserver --noreload
choices.why: That serves requests, which is what you wanted to avoid.

choices.text: check
choices.why: Right. It loads the project and reports problems without serving.

choices.text: shell
choices.why: It opens Python with the project loaded; it reports nothing on its own.

prompt: What does Django do when DEBUG is False and ALLOWED_HOSTS is empty?

choices.text: It refuses to start
choices.why: Right: CommandError, You must set settings.ALLOWED_HOSTS if DEBUG is False.

choices.text: It answers every host, with a warning in the log
choices.why: That is what the check exists to prevent.

choices.text: It falls back to localhost only
choices.why: There is no fallback; it refuses.

choices.text: It switches DEBUG back on for safety
choices.why: Turning debugging on would be the opposite of safe.

prompt: agenda changed TIME_ZONE to America/Sao_Paulo with USE_TZ = True. What happens to a date already stored?
hint: Where are dates kept, and where are they converted?

choices.text: It is rewritten in the new zone at the next migrate
choices.why: Nothing stored changes.

choices.text: Nothing; it stays in UTC and is shown in the new zone
choices.why: Right. Conversion happens only on display.

choices.text: It moves three hours, since São Paulo is UTC-3
choices.why: It is shown three hours earlier; the stored value does not move.

choices.text: It becomes invalid until converted by hand
choices.why: Stored UTC values remain valid.

prompt: You create an app with startapp but forget to add it to INSTALLED_APPS. What is the consequence?
hint: Django only knows apps it was told about.

choices.text: startapp undoes itself the next time runserver starts
choices.why: Nothing is undone; the folder stays.

choices.text: Django treats it as an ordinary folder: no tables, no templates found
choices.why: Right. Its views can still be imported by a urls.py, but Django does not manage it.

choices.text: Every request answers 500
choices.why: Unregistered apps break nothing by themselves.

choices.text: check refuses the project
choices.why: check passes; it cannot know you meant to register it.

prompt: When is a part of a Django project worth splitting into its own app?

choices.text: When a file passes a few hundred lines
choices.why: Size is not the test; a job and tables are.

choices.text: As soon as there are two models
choices.why: Two related models usually belong together.

choices.text: When it has a job named in one sentence, and tables of its own
choices.why: Right: events now, and payments if the site ever charges.

choices.text: Never; one app per project is the rule
choices.why: Large projects have many apps; agenda just does not need more.

prompt: A request for /events/a%20space/ answered 404, and the view never ran. Why?

choices.text: A space is not allowed by the slug converter
choices.why: Right. No pattern matched, so no view was called.

choices.text: The view raised Http404 because no event has that slug
choices.why: That was no-such-event, which did reach the view.

choices.text: curl sent the space unencoded and the server dropped the request
choices.why: curl sent %20; Django decoded and compared it.

choices.text: APPEND_SLASH redirected it somewhere else first
choices.why: The path already ended in a slash.

prompt: Match each path converter to what it matches.
Why name a pattern events:detail instead of writing /events/<slug>/ wherever a link is needed?
hint: What happens when the address changes?

choices.text: Named patterns match faster
choices.why: Matching speed does not depend on the name.

choices.text: Django refuses a URL written as a string
choices.why: It accepts strings; it just cannot keep them in step.

choices.text: Changing the address is one edit in urls.py, and every link follows
choices.why: Right. reverse builds the path from the name.

choices.text: Only named patterns appear in the 404 page
choices.why: Every pattern appears there.

prompt: A mobile client POSTs JSON to /events/django-night without the final slash. What does it get?
hint: Who adds the slash, and what does a redirect carry?

choices.text: The view, because Django adds the slash before routing
choices.why: Django answers with a redirect, it does not rewrite the request.

choices.text: A redirect, and the body is not forwarded
choices.why: Right. That is why APIs are called with the slash.

choices.text: A 404, since only GET is redirected
choices.why: CommonMiddleware's redirect is not limited to GET, but a POST body is lost in it.

choices.text: A 405, because the pattern ends in a slash
choices.why: 405 is about methods, not slashes.

prompt: What does a Django view receive and return?

choices.text: A URL string, and a dictionary Django serialises
choices.why: That is closer to FastAPI's style.

choices.text: An HttpRequest, and an HttpResponse
choices.why: Right. JsonResponse is a kind of HttpResponse.

choices.text: The raw bytes of the request, and bytes to send
choices.why: That is the WSGI layer underneath.

choices.text: Nothing; it writes to the socket directly
choices.why: Views never touch the socket.

prompt: In event_list, what does request.GET.get('venue') return when the URL has no ?venue= at all?

choices.text: An empty string
choices.why: An empty string comes from ?venue= with nothing after it.

choices.text: It raises KeyError
choices.why: Indexing with [] would; .get does not.

choices.text: None
choices.why: Right, and the comprehension keeps every event.

choices.text: The string 'None'
choices.why: Python's None, not a string.

prompt: An OPTIONS request to the function view with @require_GET answered 405. What did the Allow header say?

choices.text: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS
choices.why: That was the class-based view.

choices.text: GET
choices.why: Right. require_GET accepts exactly one method.

choices.text: OPTIONS
choices.why: OPTIONS was refused.

choices.text: There was no Allow header
choices.why: A 405 names the allowed methods.

prompt: Nothing in the HTTP request carries a user object, yet a view can read request.user. Where does it come from?

choices.text: Middleware attaches it from the session cookie
choices.why: Right. AuthenticationMiddleware does it before the view runs.

choices.text: The browser sends a User header with every request
choices.why: There is no such header.

choices.text: The URL converter builds it from the path
choices.why: Converters build view arguments, not request attributes.

choices.text: runserver logs the user in automatically while DEBUG is on
choices.why: DEBUG logs nobody in.

prompt: Put these in the order they happen for one GET that reaches the view.
hint: Down through the list, then back up.
items: the URL resolver picks the view

prompt: A POST to the detail URL answered 403, not the 405 that require_GET gives. Why?
hint: Which runs first: middleware or the view's decorator?

choices.text: require_GET answers 403 for POST and 405 for the other methods
choices.why: It answers 405 for every refused method.

choices.text: CsrfViewMiddleware refused it before the view was reached
choices.why: Right. The log said: Forbidden (CSRF cookie not set.)

choices.text: TimingMiddleware rejects requests with a body
choices.why: It only measures, and it timed the refusal.

choices.text: The event is read-only while DEBUG is on
choices.why: DEBUG makes nothing read-only.

prompt: You move TimingMiddleware to the bottom of MIDDLEWARE. What does its number measure now?
hint: It wraps only what is below it.

choices.text: The same as before, since all middleware run anyway
choices.why: They run, but outside its clock.

choices.text: Nothing; it must be first to work
choices.why: It works anywhere; what it measures changes.

choices.text: Mostly the view, without the other layers
choices.why: Right, and a CSRF refusal would no longer be timed.

choices.text: The time the server spent reading the socket
choices.why: No middleware sees the socket.

prompt: The class EventDetailView defines only get. What does an OPTIONS request to it answer?
hint: View implements one method for every class.

choices.text: 405, like the function with require_GET
choices.why: The class answered 200.

choices.text: 404, because there is no options method in the file
choices.why: View provides options() itself.

choices.text: 200, with Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS
choices.why: Right. HEAD comes free with get.

choices.text: 500, since options is abstract
choices.why: It is implemented, not abstract.

prompt: When is a class-based view worth its indirection, according to the lesson?

choices.text: Always; functions are the old style
choices.why: Django's own documentation keeps functions for views that do one thing.

choices.text: When Django already wrote the view you need
choices.why: Right. ListView, DetailView and friends, configured instead of written.

choices.text: When the view must answer GET
choices.why: Functions answer GET just as well.

choices.text: Only when it returns JSON
choices.why: Classes return any response.
